quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. You will notice tire failure by sudden changes in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: You should use more space between you and other vehicles when:
questions.explanation: Keep a two-second distance behind other vehicles. Increase this distance when road conditions are wet or icy, since it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs show traffic rules that you must follow.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is ______ or higher.
questions.explanation: For people age 21 or older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means they are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Safe motorcyclists know they are safest when they are:

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Safe riders are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, and turn signals. Position your motorcycle to be more visible.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed
Shoes that stop below the ankle

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Boots should be tall and sturdy to support your ankles. Heels should be low to avoid catching on foot pegs. Leather or durable material gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should ride in:
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in a staggered formation normally. When taking curves, turns, entering highways, or leaving highways, switch to a single-file formation.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of the motorcycle's braking power
Provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power
Should only be used when the road is wet
Should be the only brake you use

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is usually the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of a lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and other conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of strong material, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Under ideal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a hazard when being passed?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors. Also be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that may be thrown by passengers who are not paying attention.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles that are moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is encouraged when traffic is heavy.
Is encouraged during the day to reduce traffic jams.
Is acceptable if you feel comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after starting to ride.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Why should you use both brakes every time you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause uneven wear.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops helps you build a habit of always using both. This habit is important in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: After entering a turn, what should you do with the throttle?

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Entering a curve at a speed that is too fast for conditions may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road entirely.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: They will definitely yield to you.

questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not see you.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the edge of your lane farthest from the passing driver?

options.text: It stops the passing driver from cutting back too early.
It makes the passing driver cut back into your lane too early.
It makes the passing driver finish passing faster.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes the passing driver cut back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far edge of your lane is dangerous. It may make the passing driver return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator stop other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane so there is not much space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that reduces your space cushion and lets others see you.
One that increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
One that puts you in more danger and lets others pass you.
One that reduces danger but requires you to follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion and helps you be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.
